notes.title: First Release&Original Price Player Compensation Announcement
notes.content:
Hello players, yesterday we announced that we will offer a significant discount of 40% on August 25th, with an expected purchase price of 40.8 yuan. However, we have previously emphasized that we will not backstab crowdfunding players. Therefore, we promise in our announcement to release free expansion packs in the future to thank everyone for their support and tolerance of 'Moon White Star Dou'.

However, due to the significant discount we offered shortly after the release, in order to compensate players who made their debut or full price purchases (limited to transaction amounts of 68 yuan and 61.2 yuan), we have decided to provide corresponding compensation measures after discussion.

Before August 24th, players who purchase at the original price or purchase at the initial discount and have played for more than two hours can receive our peripheral blind boxes. The peripheral blind box includes three bars, two keychains, and one signboard, whichever is random.

And in order to give back to the players who have been with us all this time, we have decided to create a brand new free DLC in the future and give it as a gift to all players as a thank you for your continuous support.

notes.title: Statement on Disputes and Summary of Development Issues
notes.content:
Hello everyone, this is Jiushi Society. We have been considering and reflecting on the recent controversies and controversies for a long time, and it took us some time to reply. The main reason is that the production team is relatively understaffed, and most of the members' energy is focused on fixing game problems and optimizing improvements. During this period, some unexpected events also occurred that we did not expect. We have received good feedback and suggestions from everyone, and we are also considering how to give everyone a proper response.
The feedback from players has indeed given us many points for reflection, and we have also reflected on what we can do for the industry or gaming environment besides gaming. So we also sorted out the pitfalls we had stepped into internally, hoping to provide assistance to future game developers.
Firstly, let me explain the controversy and discussion, mainly focusing on the following issues:

[h2] 1. Pricing of the product [/h2]

The pricing issue of the Moon White Star Dou is also the most fiercely discussed topic among everyone. On the one hand, our pricing based on text volume and workload is too one-sided. On the other hand, due to the limited number of personnel and relevant experience in distribution, as well as a lack of market research, there is a blank market for multi-threaded long form content in China, and there is no reference pricing, resulting in unsatisfactory prices. Many players are deterred by the price.
Therefore, after further discussion, we have decided to offer a significant discount of 40% on "Moon White Star Fight" on August 25th, with an estimated final price of 40.8 yuan. Due to the mechanism of Steam, pricing cannot be directly modified in the near future. Therefore, a discount method has been adopted. The maximum discount period for Steam is two weeks, which will start on August 25th and end on September 8th. We hope that interested parties can purchase during the discount period. In order to compensate for the initial mispricing, we have decided to launch a free expansion pack in the future to thank everyone for their support and tolerance towards' Moon White Star Fight '.

[h2] II. Reply to Relevant Issues [/h2]

We have taken good notes and reflected on the controversies and issues that are currently being discussed intensively, and are discussing them while working to fix the problems. Due to the lessons learned from the past, we need to carefully consider and discuss in detail before issuing this announcement. On the one hand, we attach great importance to being able to respond to everyone's questions as an official voice, and on the other hand, we also learn from it.
Reasonable criticism and suggestions from senior creators and fellow players from all sides, reflecting deeply on the work nodes from the early stages of the project to the present. For the issues that we can modify, we will strive to make adjustments. For the issues that we are currently unable to modify, we will summarize our experience in avoiding pitfalls, hoping to provide some help for our partners who will enter the game production industry in the future.
If you have any other suggestions or criticisms, you can also raise them directly to us through various channels. We sincerely hope that those who do not like this game will not direct negative emotions towards players other than the production team.

The following is a summary of the difficulties and problems we encountered from producing "Moon White Star Fight" to its release. We also plan to make a statement here to clarify the right and wrong, and to warn those who come forward.

[h2] First pitfall: Insufficient preparation work [/h2]

Before making 'Moon White Star Fight', except for the first two main promoters who were not professionals in the game production field, everyone wanted to do GAL purely out of passion. Everything was also exploratory for the first time, so they were not fully prepared in various aspects. For issues such as product positioning, art style, and final pricing, the entire production team lacks market research. These problems have been a constant concern for us since the release of our game.

[h3] Problem 1: Lack of experience in market research [/h3]

At the beginning of the project, the production team did not attach importance to and conduct detailed market research, although they were aware of the lack of long-term daily content in the market. However, we did not deeply consider why there was a lack of content from the production team in this area, nor did we conduct in-depth exploration and detailed story positioning of the work, resulting in us not being able to clearly identify the strengths and features of the work in our subsequent work, and the game's characteristics were not effectively and specifically expressed. So much so that after several rounds of rework, it seriously slowed down the production cycle and work progress.
We also made the same mistake in the final pricing issue, as we did not conduct extensive comparative research on the pricing of similar products, which led us to arrogantly determine the price of the game. We acknowledge everyone's criticism and will work hard to remedy the mistakes we have already made, offering discounts to our fellow players in the future.

[h3] Question 2: Mistake in finalizing art style [/h3]

We have also carefully listened to and reflected on the criticism of art style. The art style of 'Moon White Star Fight' was determined by the production team, mainly referring to works of the same type on the market, without considering the art teacher's preferred style. Instead, it was decided to have the art teacher undergo a style transformation. Due to the fact that the art work for this work had already begun at the time of project approval, when the script and setting had not yet been completed, the subsequent art workload also had to be reworked and increased. The increased workload made the allocation of time and resources before going live more urgent.

[h3] Problem 3: Incorrect estimation of workload [/h3]

As a new production team, although we have captured the lack of long form and multi line daily themes in the domestic market, from the current situation, the small production team should not rashly pursue long form and multi line works for the first time. The incorrect volume may lead to tight production schedules and inability to control production effectiveness, as well as insufficient exploration of character scripts. The new work should start with a small investment in short stories, and after accumulating experience, you can try adding character lines in the form of DLC. We will also learn from our mistakes in the future, starting with short stories and taking small steps on a thousand mile journey.

[h3] Issue 4: Lack of mature project schedule management [/h3]

In fact, at the beginning of the project, the division of labor and refinement of content were done well. However, due to the increase in new content encountered during the process, the complexity of new processes, and the need to solve new problems, the gradual shortage of manpower and members' lack of work experience have been put on the table, resulting in ineffective progress of the work schedule and insufficient time for urgent testing in the future.

[h3] Question 5: Incorrect program selection and failure to handle contingency plans [/h3]

For the selection of the game engine, as the animation is also completed by the art teacher alone and needs to be integrated with the program, we chose the Cocos engine, which is more familiar to the art teacher but not used for making PC games, resulting in a large number of unpredictable program problems in the later stage. We deeply apologize for this.

[h2] Second pit: The proportion of funds and recruitment management issues of personnel [/h2]

[h3] Question 1: The proportion of investment in game production [/h3]

The vast majority of the funding for our game production this time comes from personal savings, and we do not have enough experience in allocating funds. We have spent too much on music and voice acting programs, and have not allocated funds reasonably to other parts.

[h3] Question 2: Personnel management and recruitment issues [/h3]

I have previously mentioned that there were two instances of program runaway during the production process. The main reason is also due to insufficient early planning and ineffective communication with the program teacher, resulting in multiple functions being reworked repeatedly and unable to be completed on time. Due to the fact that most members of the production team did not have relevant experience in game production, they needed to learn and familiarize themselves from scratch, often making mistakes and requiring repeated modifications and production. Each person held multiple responsibilities, making it difficult to allocate work reasonably.

[h2] Third pit: Small test sample leads to incorrect judgment [/h2]

Due to insufficient content in the demo and the failure to disclose the official version price, there were errors in estimating the quality and price, and timely modifications were not made. In addition, the lack of initial market research and planning resulted in incorrect judgments.

[h2] Fourth pitfall: Operational favoritism leading to polarization of information received by buyers [/h2]

[h3] Problem 1: Insufficient manpower was arranged to answer questions and clarify doubts when the game was launched [/h3]

Because there were too many problems in the early stages of the launch, all the production staff worked overtime to fix them. They could only reply to feedback issues in the group during their break time, and were unable to view more feedback information on the public platform in a timely manner, resulting in players who were not in the group not receiving timely responses.

[h3] Problem 2: The slow release of official news and content has led to more disputes and players not stopping in a timely manner. [/h3]

We didn't respond immediately because all members went to fix bugs, fix problems in the game, and the large number of bugs generated during the release, as well as feedback from the group, left us with no room to deal with the issues. Everyone was working on every aspect of fixing the problems. Due to our lack of spare capacity to handle issues with players outside the group, there has been a heated debate between the two sides. Some players have been affected to varying degrees by speaking positively or having feedback about the game, which is our negligence. Thank you very much to some fans for liking our Moon White Star Fight, and also to some players for their feedback. I also apologize to all the players who have been affected, very sorry. We reflect that we should respond faster in guiding public opinion, resolving disputes, and avoiding problems from getting bigger.

At this point, this' self punishment edict 'can be considered finished, but our game and production team are not yet finished. After more than a year of hard work, the dust has settled. I still remember when I urged everyone that if the game could be released, it would be considered successful. Now that the game has been released, it has been full of twists and turns, which has given us, as a new production team, a vivid and vivid game release lesson. Everyone pointed out our shortcomings and omissions, told us mistakes and areas for improvement, and left us homework after class. The road through Xiongguan is as solid as iron, and now I am stepping forward from scratch. We will learn from this lesson and continue to do a good job in the future.

Nine, the second most precious stone is jade. Although it may not be as exquisite and flawless as jade, it also has the perseverance of stone.
